slides.heading: Kadanes Algorithm
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Kadanes Algorithm, a medium famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: The best subarray ending here is either this element alone or it extends the best ending at the previous index.
slides.narration: The best subarray ending here is either this element alone or it extends the best ending at the previous index.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: all subarrays → O(n²) (O(n³) naive)
Divide and conquer → O(n log n)
Kadane: best ending here → O(n), O(1)
slides.narration: Summing every subarray is quadratic. Divide and conquer is n log n. Kadane's algorithm keeps the best sum ending at each index: either extend the previous run or start fresh, which is linear with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Max of element or element plus running
slides.narration: Step by step. First, running best ending here. Second, max of element or element plus running. Third, track the global max.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Cur and best start at the first element. For each next element, cur becomes the max of the element alone or cur plus the element, and best tracks the max of cur.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: All negative → the largest single element
slides.narration: If everything is negative, the answer is the largest single element, which is why we initialise with the first element rather than zero.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Follow-ups return the start and end indices, handle circular arrays, or extend to two-dimensional submatrices.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: The best subarray ending here is either this element alone or it extends the best ending at the previous index.
